title: The Unfinished Dictionary
epigraph: Every dictionary is a house. I closed one door.

fragments.source: A torn leaf in the lexicographer’s hand
fragments.text: Where a thing is missing, I am what remains: not nothing — the shape that nothing takes.
fragments.interpretation: Ellery reads it twice. “A word that means an absence, then. Not a thing, but a missing. Very few words dare to mean a hole.”

fragments.source: Brass plate beneath the Entrance Hall clock
fragments.text: Six candles burned on his desk at the end. “One for each letter,” he told the house, “and I shall put them out myself.”
fragments.interpretation: Ellery taps the plate. “Plainly: the word has six letters. He was never careless with a number.”

fragments.speaker: bramble
fragments.source: Mrs. Bramble, over morning tea
fragments.text: “Six candles at his desk, always six. Near the end he let one gutter out each night — and I never dared relight them.”

fragments.source: A torn leaf in the lexicographer’s hand
fragments.text: The copyist blinks above his candle, and his sentence steps mid-breath onto air. I am that step. I am that air.
fragments.interpretation: Ellery smiles faintly. “Scribes had a word for a break in a manuscript — a passage the copyist lost. He is quoting his own trade at you.”

fragments.source: Pricked into the Linen Closet doorframe
fragments.text: Somewhere inside it, an A — a tent pitched over nothing, a ladder with one rung. Where it stands I have not said, and shall not.
fragments.interpretation: Ellery inks a small green tick. “The letter A is in the word. Not first, not last, not how many times — only present. Generous and stingy in the same breath, which was entirely his way.”

fragments.source: Pinned in the Darkroom, above his case of type
fragments.text: The compositor keeps one box of nothing at his elbow, and it is the busiest box on the bench. I am the letter he sets most often, and I have no face.
fragments.interpretation: Ellery turns it to the lamp. “Printers call them quads and spaces — real metal, weighed, filed beside the alphabet. He is telling you a gap is a thing you can pick up. That is not a metaphor. That is a trade.”

fragments.speaker: posy
fragments.source: Posy, sorting the evening post
fragments.text: “His last letter went out with one word cut clean from it — a little window in the paper. You could read the whole sentence around the hole. I believe that was rather the point.”

fragments.source: Scratched inside the Library windowsill
fragments.text: Call me WORDSMITH no longer. What I took shares not one letter with that name.
fragments.interpretation: Ellery writes the name out and strikes it through. “Then W, O, R, D, S, M, I, T and H appear nowhere in the word. That is nine letters gone from your alphabet.”

fragments.source: Loose in the Study, among his unfinished entries
fragments.text: In my mother Latin I was a little pool — a hollow where the rain remembered what the ground forgot.
fragments.interpretation: Ellery goes very still. “Mother Latin. A little pool, a hollow. The word crossed into English still wearing its Latin dress — when you find it, it will look Latin. Hold that thought like a candle.”

fragments.speaker: fern
fragments.source: Fern, by the west beds
fragments.text: “There is a bed in the west garden where nothing grows. He would stand at it an hour at a time. Said there was a word for that exact shape of missing — and that he meant to see it filled again.”

fragments.source: Notched along the Counting House measuring-rule
fragments.text: There is an ell in it. Elbow to fingertip, the draper’s measure — he was pleased past all reason that a letter could also be a length.
fragments.interpretation: Ellery laughs once, briefly. “An ell is an L said aloud. So the word contains an L. Where, he does not say — only that it is in there somewhere, being measured out.”

fragments.source: A torn leaf in the lexicographer’s hand
fragments.text: Reach along a shelf in the dark. Your hand finds me before it finds one title, and you know at once which book is out.
fragments.interpretation: Ellery does not look up. “Thirty years I have known this room by its gaps, and I resent him for saying it better. A shelf tells you what is absent long before it tells you what is there.”

fragments.speaker: ellery
fragments.source: Ellery, at the catalogue drawers
fragments.text: “He asked me to reserve a shelf-mark for an entry he had not written yet. I did. It is still empty, still labelled, and I still dust it. That is not sentiment. That is cataloguing.”

fragments.source: Struck into the lead of the Conservatory rain-gauge
fragments.text: It carries a U — the cup of the alphabet, the one letter built to hold what is poured into it. Something in this word is being kept.
fragments.interpretation: Ellery: “The word contains a U. That is all it says and all it means — though mind what he chose to say it on. A thing made to measure whatever collects in a hollow.”

fragments.source: A torn leaf in the lexicographer’s hand
fragments.text: The moth eats a word from the page and leaves me behind as the payment.
fragments.interpretation: Ellery: “Moth-eaten pages, missing text. It is the scholar’s word for the gap the moth leaves behind — librarians grieve it by name.”

fragments.speaker: ellery
fragments.source: Ellery, among the reading lamps
fragments.text: “He told me once that in all the dictionary there is exactly one word that names the hole it would leave behind. Then he went and made it true.”

fragments.source: Carved on the Gallery lintel
fragments.text: It begins as LULLABY and LANTERN begin — with the tall letter, the candlestick.
fragments.interpretation: Ellery: “The first letter is L. He did love an L — half his marginalia lean on one. And you already knew one was in there; now you know where it stands.”

fragments.source: Loose in the Study, among his unfinished entries
fragments.text: A wall is only stubbornness until somebody cuts a door in it. I am the cut. Everything that ever came in, or went out, came through me.
fragments.interpretation: Ellery reads it twice, slowly. “That is a defence, dear. A gap made on purpose is a doorway — and he entered it in his own dictionary years before anyone thought to accuse him of anything.”

fragments.speaker: posy
fragments.source: Posy, at the returns pigeonhole
fragments.text: “He franked one envelope a week to an address that is not anywhere. I sent them all — we carry, we don’t decide. Every one came back marked ‘no such place’, and he filed every one like proof.”

fragments.source: Inked on the flyleaf of the dictionary he never finished
fragments.text: I began a FOREWORD to it once and got no further than the title. Not one letter of that word appears in this one. I saw to that.
fragments.interpretation: Ellery strikes the letters through. “F, O, R, E, W, D. Four of those went with WORDSMITH, so what this truly buys you is F and E — and at this stage of the plate, two letters is a great deal.”

fragments.source: Blotted on the Study’s desk-pad, read back in the glass
fragments.text: Seek me in ledgers, in memory, in a row of teeth: wherever something was, and is not, and is missed by its own outline.
fragments.interpretation: Ellery: “Anatomists borrow it too — for small hollows in bone. One word, and every science of missing pays it rent.”

fragments.source: Etched around the Study inkstand
fragments.text: One letter enters it twice, like a guest who cannot keep away. Every other letter calls only once.
fragments.interpretation: Ellery: “Exactly one letter is doubled somewhere in the word; the rest appear a single time each. That halves what is left of your list, and it is the half with the pool in it.”

fragments.speaker: bramble
fragments.source: Mrs. Bramble, in the doorway of his study
fragments.text: “I turned out his study the week after. One drawer held nothing but a label in his own hand, gone over with the pen till the paper gave. I’ve kept that drawer empty since, pet. It seemed the only tidy thing left.”

fragments.source: A rubbing from the Conservatory arch
fragments.text: Its breath runs A, then U, then A — exhale, hollow, exhale. All the rest of it is consonant bone.
fragments.interpretation: Ellery: “Its vowels, in order, are A, U, A — three, and no others. So no E, no I, no O anywhere in it.”

fragments.source: A torn leaf, folded small, in the pocket of a coat on the landing
fragments.text: The house is not quieter without him. It is exactly as loud, and one voice short. Those are not the same thing, and I am the difference between them.
fragments.interpretation: Ellery closes her eyes. “There it is. Not silence — a subtraction. He could define the ache and never once write the plain word for it, and I intend to stay cross about that for another thirty years.”

fragments.source: Cut into the Sanctum door itself
fragments.text: Somewhere in it, a hard C — cut like a keyhole. He carved this line the night the sixth candle went out.
fragments.interpretation: Ellery: “It contains a C. Carved into the very door — he wanted it found, at the end. Two words stood on your plate a moment ago. Now there is one.”

fragments.source: The last leaf in the Study’s word-book, face down
fragments.text: A dictionary keeps my chair forever empty. Speak me at the door, and I will sit.
fragments.interpretation: Ellery closes the journal softly. “He built the door to want the word itself. Name the gap, and it is a gap no longer. That is the whole of his apology, I think.”

fragments.speaker: portrait
fragments.source: The Portrait, unprompted, just once
fragments.text: “I did not destroy it. I unhoused it. There is a difference — and the difference is the word.”

letters.subject: On the matter of your journal
letters.body:
Dear newcomer,

Welcome to the manor. The house files things — a torn page, a carved line, something one of us lets slip. It all goes into your journal on its own; you need only do the noticing.

The door at the top wants no key. It wants a word, spoken once a day, and it is patient about wrong ones. Nor need you climb to say it: there is a brass speaking tube in the entrance hall, by the door, and it carries the same one word a day up to the same door.

— Posy, Post Room

letters.subject: A loose leaf, returned
letters.body:
I found this tucked into the returns tray, in his hand, torn from the same leaf as the fragment you filed. I have taken the liberty of pressing it flat.

He wrote his definitions like letters to someone who had already forgotten him. Read this one aloud, slowly — his meanings live in the pauses.

— E.

letters.subject: From between the pages of my flower book
letters.body:
Found this pressed between the campion and the sweet-pea — a charcoal rubbing he took of the Conservatory arch, years back. The arch has weathered; the rubbing hasn’t.

He rubbed it the way you’d take a keepsake of a face. Whatever is written on it mattered to him. Mind the charcoal on your cuffs.

— Fern

letters.subject: The letter with the window in it
letters.body:
I kept it. I oughtn’t have — post is post — but the last letter he ever gave me to send had a word cut out of it, neat as a stamp, and I could not bring myself to let it leave the house incomplete.

I enclose it now. Hold it to the light: you can read the whole sentence around the hole. He wanted the hole read too, I think.

— Posy

letters.subject: Something for the hand, not the eye
letters.body:
The returns tray again. I begin to think it is in league with you, and I have decided not to investigate.

Read this one standing up, in the stacks, with the lamp off. He wrote it for the hand rather than the eye and it does not survive being read at a desk. I have tested this. Twice, and both times I had to sit down afterwards.

— E.

letters.subject: Out of a coat pocket, of all places
letters.body:
I have brushed that coat every spring for thirty years and never once put a hand in the pocket. Rules, pet. Then this morning there was a corner of paper showing, which I choose to read as the house running out of patience with me.

It has been folded small enough to be carried a long while. Sit down for it. There is fruit cake, and there is the window seat, and neither of them minds waiting.

— Mrs. B.

letters.subject: Found under the mail tray, dear
letters.body:
This was under the mail tray this morning, of all places — no stamp, no sender, just your name in pencil. The house does this, you know, when it thinks a search has gone quiet too long. It seemed to want finding.

I’ve filed the enclosure in your journal already. Do come by; the kettle’s on.

— Posy

letters.subject: Again, under the tray
letters.body:
Again! Under the tray, same pencil, same nothing-else. I begin to suspect the house keeps its own postal service for slow evenings, and I try not to take it personally.

The enclosure is in your journal. Whatever it is you’re circling, dear — you are closer than the quiet makes it feel.

— Posy

letters.subject: The morning after
letters.body:
I went up at first light and the door stood open, and the six candles on his desk were lit. All six. I did not light them.

The house is warmer today — you’ll have noticed. Whatever else he was, he was waiting to be contradicted, and you did it kindly, which is the only way it could be done.

Breakfast is on the sideboard. You’ve earned the window seat.

— Mrs. B.
